caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.

The chart is a line plot illustrating the performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number", has a logarithmic scale, ranging from 0 to 10^3, with tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", has a linear scale, ranging from 40 to 65, with tick labels at intervals of 5. There are six data series, each representing a different editing method: Base (black, circle marker, solid line), FT (blue, triangle marker, solid line), IKE (red, triangle marker, solid line), MEND (brown, diamond marker, solid line), MEMIT (purple, triangle marker, solid line), and ROME (green, square marker, solid line). The Base model starts at approximately 38% and increases to around 44% as the co-occurrence number increases. The FT model's accuracy rises from about 40% to 48%. IKE's accuracy improves from roughly 44% to 50%. MEND's accuracy increases from approximately 45% to 57%. MEMIT's accuracy grows from around 40% to 55%. ROME's accuracy starts at about 51% and reaches 66%. All six lines show an overall increasing trend as the co-occurrence number increases.
